entries.name: WIS-TD(lambda)
entries.definition: A linear off-policy state-value prediction algorithm that combines component step sizes from feature usage, a scaled Dutch eligibility trace and provisional weights to implement its specified forward target with importance weighting.

definition_evidence.locator: Section 5, author PDF pp. 5–6, Equations 17–27 and Theorems 5–6; Appendix A.7, p. 18, Algorithm 1.

claims.statement: WIS-TD(lambda) is a linear state-value prediction algorithm for a target policy pi using transitions sampled from a behavior policy b. It uses V_t(s)=theta_t^T*phi(s), rho_t=pi(A_t|S_t)/b(A_t|S_t), state-dependent discount gamma and bootstrapping lambda in [0,1], and component step sizes derived from a feature-usage estimate. The source constructs its forward target from WIS-SGD-2; the method is not an action-selection or policy-improvement rule.

evidence.locator: Sections 3 and 5, author PDF pp. 3–6: linear policy-evaluation setting and importance ratios on pp. 3–4, lambda domain on p. 5, Equation 17 and the WIS-TD(lambda) forward view, Equations 18–21, on p. 6.

claims.statement: Write elementwise multiplication as ⊙, let a_t=1-eta*(phi_t⊙phi_t), and let q_t=gamma_t*lambda_t. Update u_(t+1)=a_t⊙u_t+rho_t*(phi_t⊙phi_t)+(rho_t-1)*q_t*(a_t⊙v_t) and v_(t+1)=q_t*rho_t*(a_t⊙v_t)+rho_t*(phi_t⊙phi_t). Both right sides use old v_t. Then set alpha_(t+1) to the componentwise reciprocal of u_(t+1), using the source convention that a reciprocal at zero is zero. Algorithm 1 initializes u_0=u_init*1, v_0=0, e_(-1)=0 and d_0=0, with chosen theta_0, u_init>=0 and eta>=0. Equation 17 additionally specifies theta_(-1)=0.

evidence.locator: Section 5, author PDF p. 6, Equation 17 initialization and Equations 22–24; Appendix A.7, p. 18, Algorithm 1. Componentwise division convention in Section 2, p. 3.

claims.statement: With b_t=alpha_(t+1)⊙phi_t and q_t=gamma_t*lambda_t, the trace is e_t=rho_t*b_t+q_t*rho_t*(e_(t-1)-rho_t*b_t*(phi_t^T*e_(t-1))). It uses the newly computed component step vector and the old trace in its inner product. This is a step-size-weighted Dutch trace; it is distinct from the provisional weight vector d_t and from an auxiliary GTD gradient-correction estimate.

evidence.locator: Section 5, author PDF p. 6, Equation 25 and the auxiliary-vector discussion after Equation 27; Appendix A.7, p. 18, Algorithm 1. Dutch-trace construction in Section 4, p. 5.

claims.statement: Let b_t=alpha_(t+1)⊙phi_t, q_t=gamma_t*lambda_t, C_t=theta_(t-1)^T*phi_t, and B_t=d_t-rho_t*b_t*(phi_t^T*d_t). Using the new e_t, update theta_(t+1)=theta_t+rho_t*b_t*(C_t-theta_t^T*phi_t)+(R_(t+1)+gamma_(t+1)*theta_t^T*phi_(t+1)-C_t)*e_t+(rho_t-1)*q_t*B_t. The provisional state is d_(t+1)=q_t*rho_t*B_t+(R_(t+1)+theta_t^T*phi_(t+1)-C_t)*e_t. Both right sides use old theta_t and d_t. The provisional innovation has no gamma_(t+1) factor in the source, and C_t preserves the preceding-weight prediction timing.

evidence.locator: Section 5, author PDF p. 6, Equations 26–27; Appendix A.6, p. 17, provisional-vector derivation; Appendix A.7, p. 18, Algorithm 1.

claims.statement: Theorems 5 and 6 identify the backward step sizes and weights with the source-defined forward constructions, for the same realized linear feature sequence, initial states and causal step choices. The forward view uses the return of Equation 17, discount- and bootstrapping-aware importance weighting in Equations 18–20, and the weight update of Equation 21. Its generalized online-equivalence construction includes a second target-difference term, which is represented by the provisional state in the backward procedure. This is correspondence to the specified finite-horizon replay.

evidence.locator: Section 4, author PDF p. 5, Theorem 3; Section 5, p. 6, Equations 17–27 and Theorems 5–6; Appendix A.3–6, pp. 13–17.

claims.statement: The backward WIS-TD(lambda) procedure uses O(n) arithmetic and O(n) vector state per transition for n dense features, instead of replaying all past forward updates at each new horizon. The usage vectors, eligibility trace, parameter vector and provisional vector have fixed dimension; the cost statement concerns this backward bookkeeping rather than feature generation or an entire control system.

evidence.locator: Section 5, author PDF p. 6, paragraph following Equation 27; Appendix A.7, p. 18, Algorithm 1; forward-replay cost discussion in Sections 3–4, pp. 4–5.

limitations: The selected identity is WIS-TD(lambda), not WIS-GTD, WIS-TO-GTD, usage-based TD, usage-based true online TD, WIS-LSTD, an isolated Dutch trace or a generic importance-sampling estimator. When all rho values are one and states and step-size conventions are matched, its theta update specializes to usage-based true online TD; this endpoint does not make the full algorithms exact aliases. The separately named variants retain their own recurrences and source questions.

Finite-horizon replay correspondence does not establish an unbiased objective-gradient step, convergence, stability, monotonic improvement, optimal policy learning or universal superiority. The source explicitly leaves convergence analysis for future work. Target-policy action support under behavior and well-defined returns, ratios and relevant moments are separate statistical requirements.

The source explicitly states that WIS-SGD-2 no longer reduces to ordinary tabular WIS. Its WIS-SGD-1 weighted-average result requires the stated one-hot, initialization and recency conditions; it must not be transferred to every WIS-named algorithm. For general overlapping features, reciprocal usage is not a full least-squares solve or a guarantee of an exact sample average, and self-normalization alone does not generally imply finite-sample unbiasedness.

Bare eta>=0 does not guarantee positive usage for arbitrary feature magnitudes. Conditions such as eta*phi_t(i)^2<=1, together with nonnegative importance weights and matched nonnegative usage initialization, support nonnegative forward usage; zero components can still occur. The source reciprocal-at-zero convention does not prove positivity, bounded steps or statistical validity. Importance ratios can exceed one, and traces and provisional weights are not coordinatewise clipped.

The old-v, old-d and old-weight dependencies and the new alpha_(t+1) timing are part of the construction. Equation 17 sets theta_(-1)=0 although Algorithm 1 does not repeat that initialization. Cancellation of the first theta correction does not make this prior prediction irrelevant to the first provisional d update. Adding a next-discount factor to the printed provisional innovation, substituting a GTD auxiliary update, or recomputing prior predictions with current weights changes the specified procedure.

The forward/backward derivation concerns the specified linear representation and matched realized feature/target sequence. Generic nonlinear or parameter-dependent feature learning does not automatically inherit it. State-value prediction is distinct from action-value control, and a lambda endpoint alone does not identify the method with every off-policy Monte Carlo construction. Dense linear bookkeeping does not imply cost only in the current nonzero features or a universal wall-clock advantage.

The declared evidence is the acquired author combined paper and Appendix A. Its first ten native-text pages match the official paper and its last eight match the official supplement; an embedded 2016 creation date is not a verified revision date. The source has bounded display issues in the Equation 12 horizon notation and nearby unrolling, the lambda-zero bootstrap illustration on p. 6, and intermediate Appendix A.2/A.6 lines. The explicit final WIS-TD recurrences remain separately identifiable; no complete proof certification, official erratum, author-code correctness or benchmark reproduction is asserted. Experimental comparisons retain their reported task, representation and parameter-search scope.

aio_mappings.rationale: The algorithm estimates policy state values from reward transitions, potentially sampled under a different behavior policy, and supplies prediction machinery used in reinforcement learning. The pinned class is a broader learning task; this is a qualified association, not exact identity, an algorithm-to-task subclass edge, action selection, policy improvement or convergence.

candidate_families.identity: A named modification of DNAM that detects a step which would cause avoidable self transitions, then jointly handles the next two focal values and remaining tail. Its transition matrix can differ from DNAM; it is not an alias of Liu MHGS.
candidate_families.positive_evidence: The whole defining section and Algorithm 5 were read. Equation 91 presents a concrete distinction: the target (6,5,4,2,1)/18 gives a DNAM self probability 1/28 at the third state, while the ZDNAM example has no diagonal probability. candidate_families.limits: The name does not promise zero self transitions when a conditional mass exceeds one half. Equation 95 supplies a counterexample to universal ZDNAM-over-DNAM efficiency domination. Source-reported eigenvalues 0.10306, -0.03639 and 0 were not recalculated here. The source efficiency-over-GS statement depends on reversible-kernel spectral theory and random variable selection; it is not a finite-run, systematic-scan or wall-clock guarantee.

candidate_families.identity: ST shifts cumulative probability towers by the maximum probability and is attributed to Suwa–Todo (2010). HST uses a half-unit shift and is attributed to Suwa (2022). UST/DST choose opposite probability orders; UDST mixes them equally. OHST is an ordered HST variant.
candidate_families.next_work: Retrieve and read original Suwa sources. Distinguish an inherited construction, ordering convention and mixture algorithm before adding records. The report notes an ordering/formula convention issue in Suwa2022 in footnote18 on p.37; compare the original before implementing.
candidate_families.limits: Tower invariance and minimum-self properties do not establish general ergodicity or variance improvement. HST/OHST can be period-two and nonirreducible for uniform distributions with an even number of values (p.49). Implementation/pseudocode was read but not audited by execution.

locators: p.43, ZFSS reordering and boundary discussion
candidate_families.identity: A finite categorical conditional sampler which moves left at an auxiliary height through probability bars, after redistributing excess mass from the highest bar. ZFSS additionally reorders a qualifying blocker beside the highest bar to eliminate avoidable self transitions. The geometric redesign differs from the existing generic slice-sampling record and its interval stepping-out/doubling variants.
candidate_families.positive_evidence: The whole original method section and both algorithms were read. Figure10 was visually inspected: for probabilities (0.1,0.2,0.2,0.05,0.45), the illustrated current-maximum self probabilities are 5/9 for the simple left-slice construction, 1/9 for FSS and 0 for ZFSS. Those are source figures, not independent calculations in this handoff.
candidate_families.limits: FSS need not achieve minimum self probability; ZFSS does according to the section. The generic construction is nonreversible, but the dominant-mass boundary uses a reversible common kernel. Algorithms explicitly handle point masses, small state spaces and zero current mass. No asymptotic-variance or runtime ordering follows solely from self-transition reduction.
next_work: Decide whether to retain FSS and ZFSS separately with an explicit structural distinction or use a family-plus-variant treatment.
Check Algorithms 8–9 agree, including zero-probability current state, ties for maximum, m<=2, dominant mass>=1/2 and no-self regular cases.
Check finite stationarity, nonreversibility and invariant conditional-to-joint composition before curating.
Use the exact 2024 source identity and assess AIO mappings; do not alias generic SliceSampling.

shared_boundaries.assessment: If a conditional state has mass p>1/2, an invariant kernel must retain self probability at least (2p-1)/p there, giving minimum overall self mass 2p-1. At the half-mass boundary the named minimum-self constructions coincide in that special case; this does not make them globally identical.
Removing individual-coordinate self transitions does not ensure ergodicity of a composed sweep. The report gives a three-binary-variable scan example which fails to visit two of eight states.
Minimal self transitions are not a universal variance-optimality certificate. Separate reversibility, irreducibility, scan schedule, asymptotic-estimator and computation-cost assumptions.
